causalModel.founding: The Argonians are an amphibious people with a port where they can sell. They work a pearl bed. They divided the beds into numbered lots as soon as the trade began to pay.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The bed lies in clear water over a firm bed inside the reef. The bed lies six to eight metres down. The harbour of Archon lies about 490 m away. A sand spit beside the bed is where the catch is landed and graded.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Diver families hold numbered lots by inheritance. Each family has a surface tender.
causalModel.pressures: The deep lots pay best. The deep lots kill divers. The tally book records both the takings and the deaths.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If foreigners learned to dive here, the lot system would collapse. The diver families teach their own.

districts.notes: A low sand spit off the headland where the catch is landed, opened, graded and tallied, with a short jetty at its tip; the four numbered lots it works lie on the bed 60-120 m east, under the tenders.

why.what: The district is the grading ground on the spit and its jetty. Crews work the lots and tenders from them.
why.whyHere: The spit is the nearest dry ground to the lots. It lies a short paddle from the bed. Archon lies about 590 m away.
why.whySpot: The district stands on the flat crown of the spit. The crown lies half a metre over the sea. It lies between the headland and the drop-off.
why.whyNeighbours: The lots lie 60-120 m east past the jetty. The headland path runs west toward the Long road and Archon.
why.playerPurpose: The crew grades the catch and keeps the tally here. The jetty is the way out to the lots.
why.microGeography: The spit is pale sand barely over the tide line. Open green water lies on three sides of it. The headland lies at its root.

parcels.orientationWhy: The rack stands along the spit. The fire and the grading baskets lie east of the rack, toward the jetty.

playerPurpose.note: The divers work the lots under the water. One came up dead on a lot she had no right to be working.
A quest dive on the deep lot starts from the grading ground.
The tally of each lot's catch is kept here. Its figures show who has been diving which lot.

why.what: The grading ground holds a drying rack, a fire, grading baskets and the tally. The crew works the canoe, the two tenders and the four numbered lots on the bed from the grading ground.
why.whyHere: The crew opens, grades and tallies the catch on dry ground. The catch then goes to Archon.
why.whySpot: The grading ground stands on the flat crown of the spit. It lies between the headland and the jetty foot.
why.whyNeighbours: The jetty is at the east end. The way to the headland leaves from the west end.
why.playerPurpose: The crew grades the catch and keeps the tally here. The grading ground owns the tenders and the lots they work.
why.microGeography: The sand is pale and lies half a metre over the sea. The crown of the spit is flat.

parcels.orientationWhy: Three dock spans run east from the spit tip. They end at a berth in a metre and a half of water.

why.what: The jetty is a short plank jetty on piles. A canoe lies at its berth.
why.whyHere: Tenders and canoes land the catch at the jetty.
why.whySpot: The jetty stands at the tip of the spit. The water deepens fastest there toward the lots.
why.whyNeighbours: The grading ground lies just west of the jetty. The lots lie east past the drop-off.
why.playerPurpose: The jetty is the way out to the lots. Visitors go out by canoe or by diving off its end.
why.microGeography: The sand shelves from 0.3 to 1.5 m deep.

routes.why: The path starts at the headland on the west edge of the place. It runs along the crown of the spit, past the fire and the grading ground, to the jetty foot.
A short spur leaves the spit path. It leads to the drying rack and the grading baskets beside it.

approaches.sequence: From the headland, two tenders show first on open water with buoys round them. The path drops onto the spit past the fire to the grading ground and the jetty.
approaches.wayfinding: One footpath runs from the headland east along the spit. It ends at the jetty foot.

approaches.sequence: From the boat route off the coast, the tender boats show first over open water. The jetty berth lies beyond them at the spit.
approaches.wayfinding: Boaters steer for the tenders, then the jetty.

combatSpaces.why: The combat space is the flat crown of the spit between the fire and the jetty foot. It is the sole open footing on dry ground.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The source is the catalogue record The Counted Lots. The record is works, aquaculture, M1. Occupants are 2-6 D1 divers and one surface tender. The record has no interior.
scaleGrounding.why: Diver families from Archon work their numbered lots by day. They work from two tenders and a canoe. The place has no building. The only built ground is the grading ground on the spit.

candidates.why: The ocean shelf off the harbour has a flat bed at 6-8 m inside a 3-6 m bar. A dry sand spit lies 60-150 m west of the lots.
The plotted anchor lies beside body.2966-1867 on the hist-heartland border.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The anchor stood at an inland swamp pool 1.2 m deep over a flat silt bed. The pool has no 6-12 m water and no reef. No port lies within reach. Portdun-Mont is 1.3 km away.
